newsitem.title: USA: Companies trying to sort out ice cream recall.
newsitem.headline: Companies trying to sort out ice cream recall.

text.p: Officials at Kmart Corp. and Kroger Co. said Wednesday they were trying to determine how many cartons of Pralines & Creme and Heavenly Hash ice cream were sold with the wrong kind of nuts in five states.

The companies announced a recall Tuesday of the two flavors of American Fare brand ice cream after they found out cartons were mistakenly labeled as containing almonds. Pralines & Creme has pecans and Heavenly Hash has peanuts, Kroger and Kmart said in a statement.

"We know where it was delivered to the stores. As to how many cartons may have actually been on display, we're still trying to sort that out," Paul Bernish, a spokesman for Kroger in Cincinnati, said Wednesday.

The recall only applies to those American Fare flavors sold in half-gallon round plastic tubs. The ice cream was on sale at 41 Super Kmart stores in Ohio, Texas, Georgia, South Carolina and North Carolina.
Kmart, based in Troy, Mich., urged Super Kmart customers who may have purchased the flavors since Jan. 9 to return them to the store where they were bought for a full refund.
American Fare is Kmart's private-label ice cream brand. The two flavors were made by Kroger Michigan Dairy in Livonia, Mich.

Kmart spokesman Stephen Pagnani said the company has not received any complaints or notice of health-related incidents connected to the ice cream. He said the recall was initiated because the pecans or peanuts could cause a severe allergic reaction in some people.
